database_summary: Relational OLTP-style dataset for a delivery platform. Core entities include stores, hubs, channels, drivers and orders/payments/deliveries. Orders are the central business event with timestamps and derived metric columns; payments and deliveries are separate tables linked to orders via order_id fields. Tables contain a mix of descriptive attributes (master data) and event/measurement rows (orders, payments, deliveries).

accepted.name: orders_base
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  order_id,
  store_id,
  channel_id,
  payment_order_id,
  delivery_order_id,
  order_status,
  order_amount,
  order_delivery_fee,
  order_delivery_cost,
  order_created_hour,
  order_created_minute,
  order_created_day,
  order_created_month,
  order_created_year,
  order_moment_created,
  order_moment_accepted,
  order_moment_ready,
  order_moment_collected,
  order_moment_in_expedition,
  order_moment_delivering,
  order_moment_delivered,
  order_moment_finished,
  -- preserve derived metric columns for downstream analysis
  order_metric_collected_time,
  order_metric_paused_time,
  order_metric_production_time,
  order_metric_walking_time,
  order_metric_expediton_speed_time,
  order_metric_transit_time,
  order_metric_cycle_time
FROM orders
accepted.description: Cleaned/preserved orders rows with canonical key columns, exposed timestamps and numeric metrics for reuse. Use this as the normalized orders relation to join to dimensions or aggregate over time. | Use for: order-level lifecycle analysis (e.g., time-to-accept, time-to-deliver); joins to payments/deliveries/stores/channels; filtering cohorts by order_status, time, or store/channel

accepted.name: payments_by_order
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  payment_order_id,
  COUNT(payment_id) AS payment_event_count,
  SUM(payment_amount) AS total_payment_amount,
  SUM(payment_fee) AS total_payment_fee
FROM payments
GROUP BY payment_order_id
accepted.description: Aggregated payment measures per order. Summarizes total payment_amount and total payment_fee and counts payment events per payment_order_id. Useful to avoid row-multiplication when joining payments to orders. | Use for: total paid and fees per order; orders with multiple payment attempts or refunds; joins to orders to compute net revenue per order

accepted.name: deliveries_by_order
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  delivery_order_id,
  COUNT(delivery_id) AS delivery_event_count,
  MAX(delivery_distance_meters) AS max_delivery_distance_meters,
  MIN(delivery_distance_meters) AS min_delivery_distance_meters,
  -- last status by alphabetic max is a deterministic proxy for latest state when timestamps are absent
  MAX(delivery_status) AS last_delivery_status,
  COUNT(DISTINCT driver_id) AS distinct_driver_count
FROM deliveries
GROUP BY delivery_order_id
accepted.description: Aggregated delivery measures per order (delivery_order_id). Summarizes count of delivery events, last delivery_status, max delivery_distance_meters and driver diversity. Helps prevent multiplication when joining deliveries to orders. | Use for: delivery reliability and distance analysis per order; identifying orders with multiple delivery attempts; joining to orders to analyze delivery impacts on metrics

accepted.name: orders_enriched
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  o.order_id,
  o.store_id,
  s.hub_id,
  o.channel_id,
  o.payment_order_id,
  o.delivery_order_id,
  o.order_status,
  o.order_amount,
  o.order_delivery_fee,
  o.order_delivery_cost,
  o.order_created_hour,
  o.order_created_minute,
  o.order_created_day,
  o.order_created_month,
  o.order_created_year,
  o.order_moment_created,
  -- store attributes
  s.store_name,
  s.store_segment,
  s.store_plan_price,
  s.store_latitude,
  s.store_longitude,
  -- hub attributes (nullable if store-hub missing)
  h.hub_name,
  h.hub_city,
  h.hub_state,
  h.hub_latitude,
  h.hub_longitude,
  -- channel attributes
  c.channel_name,
  c.channel_type,
  -- aggregated payment/delivery measures
  p.payment_event_count,
  p.total_payment_amount,
  p.total_payment_fee,
  d.delivery_event_count,
  d.max_delivery_distance_meters,
  d.min_delivery_distance_meters,
  d.last_delivery_status,
  d.distinct_driver_count
FROM orders o
LEFT JOIN stores s ON o.store_id = s.store_id
LEFT JOIN hubs h ON s.hub_id = h.hub_id
LEFT JOIN channels c ON o.channel_id = c.channel_id
LEFT JOIN payments_by_order p ON o.payment_order_id = p.payment_order_id
LEFT JOIN deliveries_by_order d ON o.delivery_order_id = d.delivery_order_id
accepted.description: Denormalized order-level relation joining orders to stores, hubs, channels, aggregated payments and aggregated deliveries. Exposes store and hub attributes and consolidated payment/delivery measures to support analytics without row multiplication. | Use for: order-level revenue and delivery analysis; store or hub level performance comparisons; filtering orders by payment/delivery consolidated signals

accepted.name: orders_latest_status_rank
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  delivery_id,
  delivery_order_id,
  driver_id,
  delivery_distance_meters,
  delivery_status,
  RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY delivery_order_id ORDER BY delivery_id DESC) AS delivery_rank
FROM deliveries
accepted.description: Per-order ranking of delivery events by delivery_id to pick a deterministic 'latest' delivery record when joining deliveries without timestamps. Exposes a delivery_rank where rank = 1 is the chosen/latest row (use downstream WHERE delivery_rank = 1 to select). | Use for: selecting a single delivery record per order for join de-duplication; analyzing last known delivery_status or driver assignment per order

accepted.name: payments_latest_by_order
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  payment_id,
  payment_order_id,
  payment_amount,
  payment_fee,
  payment_method,
  payment_status,
  RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY payment_order_id ORDER BY payment_id DESC) AS payment_rank
FROM payments
accepted.description: Per-order ranking of payment events by payment_id to select a deterministic representative payment record. Exposes payment_rank where rank = 1 indicates the chosen payment row for joining when per-order multiplicity exists. | Use for: joining a single representative payment per order; inspecting latest payment_method or payment_status per order
